terra.problem: The claim about Susa in the earlier part of Nehemiah's story is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The text says Sanballat and Geshem planned harm, but does not say they were smiling.
The passage does not say Nehemiah was on the wall or that he went back to work after sending his reply.
The same reply does not establish that Nehemiah never lost his cool.
The passage says Nehemiah gave the same reply, but does not provide all four replies to establish that they used exactly the same words.
An unsealed letter was not necessarily open. The passage does not establish that anybody could read it along the way.
Unsealed does not necessarily mean the letter was not closed up. The passage also does not state what the writer wanted readers to catch.
A king does not necessarily mean a revolt. The passage also does not say Sanballat wanted the rumor to spread.
King and priest are not close in sound, so the opening comparison does not make sense.
The passage gives Nehemiah's reply but does not say he was calm.
Shemaiah suggests shutting the temple doors, not locking them.
The passage does not say Tobiah was behind Sanballat's earlier letter.
The passage says Shemaiah was hired, but does not establish whether he had picked up or believed a rumor.
The passage does not say enemies were sending invitations and letters throughout all fifty-two days.
The cookie joke introduces weather without a clear connection to the work or its duration.
The joke about round numbers does not make logical sense: a round number is not something people choose based on how much opposition they face.
The claim that forty comes up often in the Bible is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say all the surrounding nations were the enemies who had been trying to frighten the Jews.
The passage does not say all the surrounding nations had been working against the wall or trying to frighten the Jews.
The verse gives two family connections in explaining the oaths, not only Tobiah's marriage into Shecaniah's family.
The nobles reported Tobiah's good deeds and exchanged information, but the passage does not call them his friends.
